Messages.Author: Sorrow

First round my prey was a weenie presence misdirect deck. He almost
ousted his prey before I ousted him. He didn't have one of his roughly
18 Misdirects when he needed it. This left me with an easy 2 VP. The
third prey went soon after. It took about four turns. Each of the
players had three plus minions. Player 4 wasted his Rat's Warnings on
his predator and spent a bunch of pool on equipment. If the presence
deck had the Misdirection that it should have had, I probably would have
been swept by it.

Round two my prey brought out Justine but then immediately intercepted a
big vamp with an agg damage dealing weapon. Oops! Justine was
diablerized by my grand predator (why? I don't know). My tactic in this
game was to influence out all four of my vampires on the third turn. My
predator had a brujah deck and I didn't want to get rushed. I hoped
that my prey would influence himself down low enough for me to bring up
all four vampires at one time and then oust him before I could get
rushed by my predator. Once my prey brought up Justine I thought I was
dead. Once Justine died I was happy. When my predator's turn came
around and he didn't rush I was even happier. I ousted my prey in one
turn. I ousted my next prey the next turn. The next guy in line beat
me down with an array of 2nd Tradition Domains and Sudden Reversals.
Also, he had damage dealing votes. When he tried to split the Con Agg
votes by placing one on his prey and 3 on me (his grand prey) I
threatened to oust myself and give his prey 6 pool and a VP. Had he not
relented I may have died with only one VP. Anyway, the winner that
round was a Vote + 2nd Trad. deck. This was a definite 0 VP game had my
prey not screwed up.

Third round. 4 player table with David Tatu (VP leader at the time) was
my grand predator/grand prey. David ousted his prey. I ousted my prey
( A brujah bruise and bleed deck that neither bruised nor bled).
David's deck was supposed to life boon and then change the table order
to deal the death blow himself. David made a calculation on how much
pool to give my prey. He didn't want to go too low on pool so he gave
my prey enough pool to handle anything but a Forshadowing Destruction.
I had one though. Had David given the guy a couple more pool I would
have had 2 fewer VPs.

In the finals I was the top seed so chose last. I put Tatu as my prey
because he only had big vamps and I thought I could get him out before
he got off a minion tap. My predator seemed to have some kind of bleed
deck. My grand predator had a bleed deck and my grand prey (the winner)
had a presense bleed deck. He also used an abundance of majesties to
have one sizable vamp block and untap with. My predator got me down
really low and David Tatu got off a Minion Tap which delayed me quite a
while. Everyone was able to develop their game. Save for David who was
nursing his one vamp trying to get off a 5th Tradition and Minion Tap
combo that would have put him out of reach.

> Same questions of the grand prey. How far down
> stream did a player have to be in order to be able to do anything with

Usually grand prey. If you played with larger vampires (not using Tomb
or Info Hwy.) then definitely grand prey.

> On the other side of the coin, how threatening was your predator, Robert,
> in each of your games? An extension of this question would be, what
> type's of decks were your Predator/Prey?

I never once had an action played on me that I wished I could block. I
was never rushed. No bleed was ever deflected.

Oh, lastly, after hearing about the Thursday tournament and the
prevalence of weenie decks I had to decide what I'd play for Saturday's
event. What I chose to do was devote a percentage of the deck to wakes
and deflections and let the weenie decks help me oust my prey. I
realized that this would slow me down so I added Gird Minions to avoid
getting intercepted while hunting. The wakes and deflects did come in
handy on occassion.

> I understand that you didn't
> actually win so at least in the finals you had to of hit some sort of snag.
> What was it?

I never played against the eventual finals winner in a prelim. I should
have made him my prey leaving David's big deck as my predator. I think
I would have either gained 3 VPs or swept had I made that choice. But,
even with our seating I was essentially beaten by a 6 Cap vampire who
woke 1 time and majestied 5 times. When you spend a lot to misdirect a
weenie horde, you cannot be blocked many times before your pool is
gone. Didn't people used to complain that the 20 majesty deck was
broken? I'd have to agree! :-)

Joe C.'s nasty intercept deck was almost solely responsible for a Weenie
Presence deck not getting into the finals. Joe C.'s deck beat the
tournament winner in a preliminary round.

No one rushed me. Only one player had any amound of wakes or 2nd
Traditions. No one hit me with votes. Only one Sudden Reversal (from
the 2nd Trad. player) No one bled me hard, Mind Raped, Corrupted,
Hostily took over, etc.

I suspect we'll soon see my player rating jump up a bit. So, let me be
proactive and take a moment to say that I've only played this deck in no
more than one out of every three tournaments. My rating is not equal to
the rating of "Weenie Misdirect Bleed". Last time I played this deck I
lost multiple games (To Anarch Revolt decks and Rush Combat decks) and
was beaten in the finals by a Low-Cap Potence Rush Deck.

It is actually tougher to defend against than S&B. There's no

> This is true. However, when you take into account that you are
> getting Misdirected every turn, it is much much worse. You can

> problem with this deck - you can prepare for a general strategy
> type (heavy S&B, etc), but unless you prepare for this specific
> deck, there is little to nothing you can do.

But some preparation that you can do is quite simple and can be
used against a variety of decks.

Sudden Reversal is one. If they can't tap you out, they won't
be able to bleed you as much. That can give you time to develop
your deck. And if you don't face a weenie deck, Sudden Reversal
is still useful.

Atonement is another good one. The trick is getting the Atoned
vampire back untapped after a Misdirection. Protean, Presence,
and Animalism (Guard Dogs and Rats' Warning say to untap)
can do that fairly easily. If you don't face a weenie deck,
there are still often small vampires you can use this against
and it can be useful for stopping vote decks. Put a gun on
this vampire and you'll stop cold any weenie deck not using
Misdirection.

Pool gain can help you survive long enough for someone to oust
the weenie. Usually, some deal making is involved to accomplish
this. However, I think most people realise that if a weenie
deck isn't killed, it will most likely sweep the table.

Mike Courtois also played a weenie bleed deck, but I'm not sure
it used Misdirection. He only faired 2 VP in the whole
tournament. Obviously, they can be stopped.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Sorrow wrote:
>>But it is my opinion that this particular deck type is worse than even
S&B...>>

Worse in what sense? In my opinion, generic Malk S+B is only moderately
effective, at best. In our local tournaments, Malk S+B decks tend to get
nowhere, and quickly. Highly dubious and complex Dominate/Protean decks do
pretty well, but your old "cheesy" S+B standby generally just gets whacked.

>>This is true. However, when you take into account that you are getting
Misdirected every turn, it is much much worse. You can plan for heavy
bleeds, even S&B by putting in some Deflections and Wakes. But you
can't deflect if you are tapped and unless you put in tons of WwEF/FA,
you can't use it. That's my biggest problem with this deck - you can
prepare for a general strategy type (heavy S&B, etc), but unless you
prepare for this specific deck, there is little to nothing you can do.>>

I agree that weenie bleed decks are powerful--probably more powerful than they
should be. However, that being said, if you are going into a tournament, it
seems prudent to build a deck that can stand up to a good weenie bleed deck, as
it is likely that you will run into one, and it isn't that hard to do:

-Weenie Pot Rush deck. Robert said he didn't run into any of these, and if he
had, he might very well have not gotten anywhere. I have played in many games
as the prey of a weenie bleed deck with my Nosferatu Rush deck. Some games I
win, some games I lose, but it is by no way a steamroller.

-Lots of untap/WWEF and deflect. If you are going to rely on deflection as a
bleed defense, you need to be able to untap. Period. Building a deck with
deflections and not an equal amount of Wakes (I'd go with 10 of each for a
reliable defense) is asking to be killed.

-Animalism/Protean defenses. Playing a Gangrel deck with Rats/Wakes and Earth
Melds (or Cat's Guidance) will go an awfully long way to stopping such a deck
dead in the water, and is perfectly viable in an offensive deck. I have a
weenie Protean bleed deck with enough Wakes and Earth Melds (as well as light
intercept and a few Attonements) to put up a very determined defense against
such a deck.

-Being just as fast. Make your own weenie bleed deck. Or a weenie Pre vote
deck. Or an inhuman waves Embrace deck (what is he going to do? Misdirect 10
vampires every turn?)

I know we had this very same discussion fairly recently, and all the same ideas
still apply--if you leave vampires untapped, hoping to block/deflect a weenie
bleed deck, you are clearly already losing. Tap out every turn (so his
Misdirections are useless) either ousting your prey or beating up your
predator's vampires. Then have reliable defenses that work when you tap out
every turn (or by tapping out every turn).

I completely agree that it is unfortunate that competetive Jyhad is so
completely affected by weenie speed decks ('cause it is). However, barring some
sort of significant rules change, this will always be the case, so you are best
off going into a competetive situation with a deck that can compete.

davey! wrote:
>>i would guess that your group has a lot of combat decks in it;
protean/dominate provides a lot more combat defense than the Malks can
get.>>

Yup. The Malks get totally killed by *any* sort of combat, as the only viable
defense thay have is various Dodges (well, that and disguised guns, but that is
a dubious angle at best). Thus, if there are any reliable combat decks sitting
near a Malk deck, it doesn't get anywhere. I susepct the reason that so many
people refer to the Malkavians as "cheesy" is because they don't play enough
combat decks.

>>actually, this one is hard to do. it's fairly hard both to design and to
play, but it's especially hard to hard to get cards for. IG and Torn
Signpost, the cornerstones of this kind of deck, are not easy to get
around here. and one tends to need a lot of them...>>

The designing has already been done, and the way to play them have been
discussed at length. I have won tournaments with my Rush deck, as has Josh
Duffin, James Hamblin, and other folks. These decks are floating around the
web. Getting all the cards necessary is a problem, true, but with boxes of
boosters costing 10 bucks a pop, and Korshavn selling uncommons for .25 each,
and an entire internet of folks to trade with, it isn't *that* hard to get the
cards you need. If you want to make a good Rush deck, you get the cards (much
like if you want to make any good deck). As competetive Jyhad tends to be
dominated by weenie speed decks, and Rush decks can compete against such decks,
if you want to be competetive in tournament Jyhad, such Rush decks might be an
option.

>>10?! wow, i would be surpised if a deck so heavily weighted against bleed
would win in a tournament...>>

If you are relying on bleed bounce as your only bleed defense, then 10 might
not even be enough. I personally wouldn't make a deck that relies only on bleed
bounce as bleed defense, but I like being more pro-active than that. However,
the point that was being made by Sorrow was that the Goudie style deck burns
through light bleed bounce with no problem, which is correct. If you plan on
stopping a weenie bleed deck with bleed bounce, you are going to need a lot of
bounce and a lot of untap.

>>This doesn't make them useless. It only gives your predator pool. If his
deck is designed to play a misdirection every turn, your tapping out does
nothing to stop him, it only lowers the price he has to pay.>>

And if the deck is designed to play a misdirection every turn, it doesn't care
that is has to pay the pool. My point is not that you gain some sort of huge
advantage by making him not have to play misdirections, it is that you are much
better off tapping out doing things that are useful, as he is going to
misdirect you anyway. If your deck spends every action it has available
destroying his vampires or gaining pool or killing your prey just as quick as
he is killing you, you are going to be far more successful than if you take no
actions, leave your vampires untapped so you can block him, and then get
surprised when he misdirects you, again.

Rahman come out, you just put them in torpor, because you KNOW what's
going to happen. Weenie Dominate is the hardest to "sneak up" on
people with, in my opinion - but far and away the most lethal and
fast. Toreador PRE bleed is probably the sneakiest since it takes a
little bit to get rolling - but it is also the most fragile.

Some decks, unfortunately, don't - one of the reasons you see
equipment getting bashed so heavily on here. It's not the equipment

before you can get that Assault Rifle out (which admittedly tends to
stop weenies very unsubtly).

> But it is also significantly more complicated to make work than

?? I'm not so sure this is the case. The deck has almost everything you
could want available to it. Form of Mist itself is an excellent card, as
it provides combat defense and sealth all a once. In general, protean
provides stealth, combat defense, combat offense, and untaps for extra
actions. Dominate provides bleed and bleed bounce as well as a host of
other useful things. You could also splash fortitutde for blood gain and
even more combat defense...
By comparison, the Malks have very little to offer. Obfuscate
gives the stealth, sure, but not all the other stuff you get from protean.
Auspex is ok, but the malks can't make such good use of it. And they get
creamed in combat...

> And it falls over to Psyche!, Fast Reaction, etc...

Fast reaction, if it even works against FoM, is a pretty weak card. In
the end, you wind up with two tapped minions, and I can just play
Earth Meld in the second combat to have no tapped minions. Then another
of my minions can bleed...
As for Psyche, yeah, it'll stop FoM, but Protean has other stealth
to offer, which should go in this type of deck. The thing about protean
that's so great is the extreme flexibility of the cards: FoM can be used
defensively to dodge or end combat, or offensively to gain stealth and tap
a minion. Rapid Change has similar flexibility. Claws can be used to
maneuver or press or torporize your opponent (which beats Psyche!...)

> not to mention that a Woken vampire is still Awake, i believe,
> he just needs to generate an extra +1 intercept. And you can only
> Form of Mist once per action...

yup, this is true. but you can still gain more stealth, and FoM should
not be the only stealth you play. and in any case, the Malks don't have a
better card to offer in this situation.

> Plus, you can make Malk bleed with a bunch of 4 and 5 caps. Caitlin
> is a 'must' for any serious PRO/DOM deck, as is Iliana, but you can't
> make an entire crypt of 2 vamps, and the other PRO/dom users are 8 and
> 9 caps... a far cry from 4 and 5.

First of all, I would say that the PRO is more important than the dominate
in this kind of deck. If you let yourself use discipline cards and
Computer Hacking, the crypt can be worked out.
Secondly, Protean provides you with cards to untap your minions,
most noteably Earth Meld and Homunculus. With these, having fewer
minions does not mean fewer actions. Plus, the combat defenses offered by
this deck generally make your vampires last longer than Malks.

Fast Reaction *does* work against FoM. No, it isn't the greatest
card, but you won't be able to Earth Meld in the 2nd combat due to
card text on FR - "During the first round, the opposing minion cannot
use any strikes." Any deck making use of FR will be sure to torporise
your minion, usually with some agg weapon (ivory bow) or other, and a
PRO/dom deck can't afford to be losing its minions temporarily this
way - its vampires are too big.

The other stealth is irrelevant. One Psyche! stops the action cold,
which makes the block successful even if you S:CE away from the combat
the second time as well - and the whole purpose of a FoM deck is to
Not Get Caught. Rapid Change has its place, but in this type of deck,
Earth Control or Earth Meld are much better alternatives (although I'd
rather just put more FoM in the deck to get the S:CE). Putting Claws
into your deck increases the blood spent by your vampires, and
guarantees that you won't be able to continue the action, defeating
the purpose of your deck again. (Also, dilutes your deck - you'll end
up noticing that you have a Claws in hand when you need a FoM.)

form of combat other than Rush combat. They don't need a card in this
situation, since they just generate +3 stealth with two cards, one of
which could even be Faceless Night (tapping the attempted blocker).
Much easier to make work properly than Form of Mist.

Since your deck -requires- being blocked, a Potence deck that is
temporarily out of rush can actually leave itself untapped and wait
for you to come to it - and survive that way, if you run out of your
alternate stealth cards. Ouch!

Then, how much alternate stealth do you put in? If nobody blocks you
(a very real possibility, and most people's standard response to any
sort of stealth/bleed), you'll hand jam promptly on Earth Controls and
FoM's. If you don't put enough in, the Wake-happy deck will get you
with its KRCG radio, Rumor Mill, or just plain Spirit's Touch (since
it didn't need intercept to block you the first time.) Trickier than
Malk S&B by a long shot, since you can almost guarantee that people
will just say "the hell with it" and quit blocking against Malks -
people seem to want to block the FoM bleeders more. Meaning that Malk
decks know not to include a WHOLE lot of stealth. =)

>> Plus, you can make Malk bleed with a bunch of 4 and 5 caps. Caitlin
>> is a 'must' for any serious PRO/DOM deck, as is Iliana, but you can't

>Computer Hacking, the crypt can be worked out.

I have a very functional PRO/dom deck, and i'm quite fond of it. From
my experience, a pile (8) of DOM discipline cards is absolutely
necessary, and you'll STILL only get out three minions, tops. Most
Malk decks work well with only a couple OBF/DOM skill cards tossed in,
so they have a lot more free master slots to include Sudden Reversals,
blood gain, Forest of Shadows, etc. Again, much easier to do with
Malks.

The PRO weenie/Computer Hacking/Laptop/FoM deck is a different
approach than PRO/dom. Much less susceptible to bounce, much easier
to produce. Requires lots more FoM, though, and highly susceptible to
people just not-blocking, since bleeds for 2 can often be ignored or
Telepathic Countered.

> Secondly, Protean provides you with cards to untap your minions,
>most noteably Earth Meld and Homunculus. With these, having fewer
>minions does not mean fewer actions. Plus, the combat defenses offered by
>this deck generally make your vampires last longer than Malks.

What other actions are you going to be taking, and what the heck do
you want to be untapped for in a sneak & bleed deck? :) Just toss in
some Wakes/Deflections, and a few Delaying Tactics if you have a vote
problem, and off it can go on its merry little way. Sure, this will
dilute your offense a little bit (although Deflections are only a
minor dilution since they also provide offense), but -some-
concessions for defense have to be made. :)

No. FoM, when used at superior by an acting vampire, is a action modifier.
Therefore the acting vampire can play superior FoM only once per action.
Defensively (used by a non-acting vampire), it doesn't modify the action,
so it doesn't count as an action modifier, so it isn't restricted.

vampire, so cannot be played more than once per action at superior.
[RTR 19980623]

A: I would not in any way describe my playgroup as ruthless, cutthroat, or play
only to win. You clearly have been missing out on a great deal that I have been
saying. My play group is competetive, yes, and by competetive, I mean that when
we play with "tournament viable" decks, we try our darndest to win, don't pull
any punches, and do our best to kill our enemies. That is because it is what
the game is designed for. Jyhad is a competetive game with very well defined
victory conditions. As has been pointed out multiple times by the likes of Fred
and myself, if all players in a given game are not playing by the same rules,
then no one has fun. The assumed rules of Jyhad are that everyone is playing to
win the game by getting the most victory points. If everyone in a given game is
not playing with this same motivation in mind, the game doesn't work. If 5
players sit down at a game of Jyhad, each with a different motivation in mind,
the game will suck. For instance, if, in a given game:

-Player A wants to win by getting the most VPs.
-Player B doesn't care about VPs, he just wants to screw Player C, regardless
of where he is sitting.
-Player C doesn't care about VPs, he just wants to see how many Garou Packs he
can get into play.
-Player D wants to get ousted as quickly as possible, so he can go play Magic.
-Player E is unconcerned with VPs, he just wants to try out his deck that
exists solely to get its predator ousted.

The game is going to suck for most players involved for various reasons. Player
A is looking for good competition, and he isn't going to get any. Player C is
going to be unfairly and arbitrarily destroyed by a player across the table.
Player B isn't going to put any pressure on his prey. Player D is going to die
very quickly, making his predator's life way too easy, making his grand
predator's life too hard. And so on. The end result of this is that mosty
players are not going to have a good time.

While this is an extreme example, the whole "I don't like cheese" viewpoint
simply isn't that different. By damning players who are playing perfectly
legal, perfectly viable decks that are encouraged by the rules of the game, you
are basically saying "I'm not playing the same game as you, but you suck for
playing by the actual rules", and consequently playing with different victory
conditions than your opponents. This results in the game sucking.

B) Yes, we have very similar decks (weenie speed bleed decks or weenie presence
speed vote) in regular rotation in our play group. When they were first
introduced into our play environment, yes, the kicked our assess over and over
again. However, rather than spending all of our effort complaining about them
and calling them cheesy (which we did do for a while...), we decided to make
decks that could compete (and were perfeclty viable regardless of the presence
of weenie decks at the table, i.e. they were not specific "anti-weenie" decks),
and we succeeded. At this point in time, when Steve brings out his weenie
bleed/Anarch revolt abomination, no one says "Steve, you suck, cheesmiester!",
we just play. Sometimes his deck wins. Sometimes it doesn't. Just like all the
other decks.

I think this statement/question is too sweeping. I don't
know that at most tournaments where there is a tap&bleed
deck, it wins. I don't think anyone has done a broad
enough survey of Jyhad tournaments to make such a
statement. And more generally, in my opinion, the Jyhad
tournament scene is not large enough that it would be
very significant if tap&bleed decks *did* win most of the
tournaments they were played at.

The problem is (again IMO) that there are not enough good
players playing good decks at enough sizable tournaments
for individual tournament results to be a reliable indication
of what is or isn't overpowered in tournament play. Because
our game doesn't have that many players, it doesn't have
that many tournaments either. And because the tournaments
aren't played for 'meaningful' prizes (money for example),
people aren't necessarily driven to search out the best
possible winning strategies.

Tap&bleed may be an abusive strategy (although I don't
think it is), but a few tournament wins for it isn't
good proof of that. Especially when there are 'flukes'
like GenCon - at one of the largest Jyhad tournaments in
the country.
